sections.title: A milder way to say "you'd better"
sections.content: English "you'd better..." carries a hint of urgency, but Hungarian's closest match, *jobb lenne, ha...* ("it would be better if..."), stays firmly in the register of advice, not warning. Like Unit 3's *szeretném, ha*, the *ha*-clause here takes the conditional mood too, even though you're talking about something that could still happen — that's just how Hungarian *ha*-clauses work when the whole sentence is hypothetical.

items.spanish: Jobb lenne, ha inkább pihennél egy kicsit.
items.english: It'd be better if you rested a bit instead. / You'd better rest a little.

items.spanish: Jobb lenne, ha elmondanád neki az igazat.
items.english: It would be better if you told him/her the truth.

sections.content: *jobb lenne, ha* is stronger than an *-hat/-het* suggestion but still gentler than a warning — it says the speaker has a real opinion about what's best, without any threat attached. Save *nehogy* (coming up in Lesson 4) for when something risky is actually at stake.
